lessons.title: Verify rg exists before trusting empty search results in the adapter container
lessons.symptom: Batched `rg -l ...` symbol searches all return empty even though the symbols clearly exist in the tree (e.g. a file listed by `ls` contains the searched keyword).
lessons.root_cause: The adapter skill mandates `rg` for symbol search, but this CI container does not have ripgrep installed; with stderr suppressed (2>/dev/null) every invocation silently returns nothing, so an adapter can wrongly conclude a commit is a no-op.
fix_guidance: First search of a step: run `which rg` (or any trivial rg) and check output before trusting results
If rg is missing, use `grep -rEn --include='*.py'` for all symbol searches
Treat a suspiciously ALL-empty result set as a signal to re-verify tool availability, not as evidence of no impact
lessons.example: step-1 (baseline da329cc303a5): initial `rg` sweeps for hf_processor_applies_updates / MambaStateShapeCalculator / short_conv all returned empty and nearly concluded a full no-op; a later `ls` exposed patch_mamba_utils.py, contradicting the empty results. Re-running with grep found the real impact set.
